drivers.text: season 'good' for the region this month
drivers.label: reasoning

details.confidence_note: flow/tide data in hand; no fresh DNR mention; water temp measured

presence.note: MD DNR: highest walleye densities 'from Dam 5 downstream to Point of Rocks' (Point of Rocks is the downstream end of that reach). No catch evidence here.

access.note: NPS Point of Rocks Boat Ramp, 3703 Canal Rd, Point of Rocks MD 21777, C&O Canal mile 48.2; auto and boat-trailer parking, vault toilet. C&O Canal Trust also notes a small lot at the train station for day and overnight use.

rules.text: Nontidal waters (MD), statewide: harvest 01-01–12-31 15 in minimum 5 per day / 10 possession
Potomac River mainstem, nontidal (MD): harvest 01-01–04-15 15-20 in slot 5 per day / 10 possession; 04-16–12-31 15 in minimum 5 per day / 10 possession
Maryland-Virginia boundary is the low-water mark on the Virginia shore; Maryland owns the riverbed (Black-Jenkins award 1877). Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virginia_v._Maryland

NPS: Maryland license required for 16+ in nontidal waters; regs follow the state where you fish. Fishing from the Virginia bank would be a separate question. Source: https://www.nps.gov/choh/planyourvisit/fishing.htm
License: Maryland nontidal license (Matt's stated license; not verified here) (per Matt; not verified)

rig.primary: 3/8 oz round jighead (2/0) with 3.5-4 in white or chartreuse paddletail/grub, 20 lb braid to 3 ft 12 lb fluoro
rig.alternate: Suspending jerkbait 4.5 in (silver/black or clown) or small shallow crankbait, 20 lb braid to 3 ft 12 lb fluoro, #1 round snap
rig.switch_trigger: Snagging every cast in rock, or fish seen chasing near the surface at dusk
rig.gear_note: Workable on Matt's 7 ft Crossfire MH (20 lb braid) with the leader dropped to 10-12 lb; ideal is a 6'6"-7' medium spinning rod with 10 lb braid. The unconfirmed 6'6" Ugly Stik fits if the 17 lb leader is swapped lighter.

drivers.label: forecast

presence.note: Park page lists 'catfish' (species not stated). Fish and Hunt Maryland lists blue catfish for Mattawoman Creek.

access.note: Smallwood State Park, 2750 Sweden Point Road, Marbury MD 20658. Day use $3/vehicle weekdays, $3/person weekends and holidays (+$2 non-residents).

rules.text: Maryland tidal waters: harvest 01-01–12-31 none none (warning: Applies to MD waters. On the tidal Potomac mainstem PRFC rules were not checked.)
Tidal Mattawoman Creek, Maryland. Not on the PRFC mainstem, so no PRFC question at the park (reasoning).
State park day-use fee applies.
License: Maryland Chesapeake Bay & Coastal Sport License (park page says required 16+). Matt states he holds MD tidal; not verified here. (per Matt; not verified)

rig.primary: 7/0-8/0 circle, 18-24 in 50 lb mono leader, #3/0 barrel swivel, 8 mm bead, 3-6 oz no-roll or pyramid on fish-finder slide, fresh menhaden or gizzard shad chunk
rig.alternate: 5/0 circle, 18 in 30 lb mono, barrel swivel, bead, 1-2 oz egg or bank sinker slide, chicken liver or cut shad
rig.switch_trigger: Only small fish or crabs stripping cut bait in 30 min, or fishing a slower tributary bank
rig.gear_note: Best on a heavy 8-10 ft catfish/surf rod with 50-65 lb braid. Matt's Rhino catfish setup with 65 lb braid (unconfirmed) or his 10 ft Penn Pursuit IV fit; the Crossfire MH is undergunned for big blues. His 4/0-5/0 circles are small for big blues - buy 7/0-8/0
